angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 438,987 km at 23.91 pc = 0.25 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 41.8223 +/- 0.0208 mas (same row, RUWE 1.25): 23.91 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.631 +/- 0.014 solar radii from Naponiello et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2443 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...693A...7N/abstract): 438,987 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.642 +/- 0.026 solar masses from Naponiello et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2443 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...693A...7N/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4375 +/- 65 K from Naponiello et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2443 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...693A...7N/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Naponiello et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2443 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...693A...7N/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2443.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.646, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
